Vehicle Schedules We generate two EV schedules as inputs to the vehicle battery model, (1) a charging availability schedule, which indicates when a vehicle is plugged in and available to charge, and (2) a driving schedule, during which the EV battery is discharging energy. Both schedules are derived from the dwelling unit’s occupancy schedule, and the driving schedule also depends on the assigned ev_hours_per_week argument. The durations of charging energy events are dependent on the charging availability schedule and the SOC. Figure 3 shows a snapshot of relevant schedules for a single EV driver. The schedules values represent the fraction of each 15-minute timestep during which the event occurs, and values less than one correspond to events shorter than 15 minutes. 4 See Section 3 of Speake et al. Illustration of a ResStock EV plugged-in schedule, charging power, driving schedule, and driver occupancy schedule The durations of driving periods scale with the occupant’s weekly driving hours and are proportionally adjusted with the duration of the away period. On average, higher-mileage drivers have shorter away periods in which they are not driving. We assume a constant driving speed but scale the discharge power based on the ambient temperature, as discussed in the following subsection. The charging schedule is similarly based on occupancy, where the baseline behavior assumes that the vehicle is plugged in when the occupant arrives home.
